The '''''Alberta Act''''' ({{langx|fr|Loi sur l'Alberta}}), effective September 1, 1905, is the [[Act of Parliament|act]] of the [[Parliament of Canada]] that created the [[Provinces and territories of Canada|province]] of [[Alberta]]. The act is similar in nature to the ''[[Saskatchewan Act]]'', which established the province of [[Saskatchewan]] at the same time. Like the ''Saskatchewan Act'', the ''Alberta Act'' was controversial because (sec. 21) it maintained the [[Government of Canada]]'s control of all of Alberta's [[natural resource]]s and [[public land]]s. Alberta did not win control of these resources until the passage of the ''[[Natural Resources Acts]]'' in 1930.

The ''Alberta Act'' defined the boundaries for the [[electoral districts]] of the [[1905 Alberta general election|first Alberta general election in 1905]].

The ''Alberta Act'' is part of the ''[[Constitution of Canada]]''.
